summary: Verified CRMEvent favicon replacement (black calendar on Tiffany background) with ?v=6 cache-buster. All 8 static assets (favicon.ico, favicon-16/32/48/192/512.png, apple-touch-icon.png 180, favicon_calendario_nero.png 725) are served with correct MIME, correct square dimensions, and ICO contains 16/32/48 sub-images. index.html head contains all required rel=icon/apple-touch-icon links with ?v=6 and no ?v=5. manifest.webmanifest exposes 192/512 icons with ?v=6 and both are reachable. Main logo (logo-crmevent.png) is unchanged and still renders on landing header and login page (naturalWidth=2000). Pixel-level sampling of favicon-512 confirms calendar palette: >10% dark pixels (black calendar) and >20% Tiffany-tone pixels (background #0ABAB5/#0CC0C0). Required a frontend restart because CRA dev server had cached the pre-change index.html in memory (served ?v=5 until restart) — after `supervisorctl restart frontend` the preview URL correctly serves ?v=6.
critical_code_review_comments: CRA dev server caches public/index.html at startup — any edits to index.html (icons, meta tags, etc.) require a frontend restart to be reflected on the live preview URL. If main agent edits public/index.html in future, remember to `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend`.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Favicon assets live in /app/frontend/public/ as favicon-{16,32,48,192,512}.png, favicon.ico (multi-size 16/32/48), apple-touch-icon.png (180), favicon_calendario_nero.png (725 source). All referenced in index.html + manifest.webmanifest with ?v=6. Regression test file: /app/backend/tests/test_favicon_assets.py. For future favicon changes bump to ?v=7 and update the test's version regex.
rca of the issue: Initial pytest run showed index.html still contained ?v=5 even though the source file /app/frontend/public/index.html had been updated to ?v=6. Root cause: craco/webpack-dev-server caches the index.html template at startup; the file was modified AFTER the frontend supervisor process started. Mitigation: `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend`, then re-ran tests — all 12 passed.
